steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **One query instead of eleven** in *SARGable queries and N+1*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: How many queries does this pseudo-code send to the database?
code: FROM (SELECT id FROM stations WHERE district = 'Docklands');
--   stations = SELECT * FROM stations WHERE district = 'Docklands'
--   for each station: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rides WHERE station_id = ?
setup: CREATE TABLE stations (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, district TEXT NOT NULL);

WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 40) INSERT INTO stations SELECT i, 'Station ' || i, CASE i % 4 WHEN 0 THEN 'Docklands' WHEN 1 THEN 'Old Town' WHEN 2 THEN 'Northside' ELSE 'Harbourside' END FROM n;

CREATE TABLE rides (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, rider_id INTEGER NOT NULL, station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES stations(id), started TEXT NOT NULL, minutes INTEGER NOT NULL, fare_cents INTEGER NOT NULL);

WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 20000) INSERT INTO rides SELECT i, (i * 7919) % 500 + 1, (i * 31) % 40 + 1, datetime('2026-01-01', '+' || ((i * 7) % 300) || ' days', '+' || ((i * 13) % 1440) || ' minutes'), (i * 37) % 55 + 2, ((i * 37) % 55 + 2) * 15 FROM n;
steps.explain: One query for the list, then one per Docklands station: 1 + 10. A single `GROUP BY` query would do it in one.

prompt: Replace the loop from the last question with **one** query: for each **Docklands** station return its **name** and number of **rides**, sorted by **name**.
Tables: `stations(id, name, district)` (40 rows) and `rides(id, rider_id, station_id, started, minutes, fare_cents)` (20,000 rows; `started` is text like `'2026-03-14 08:05:00'`).
